nodes.name: prime_field_mod_of_equal
nodes.summary: Equality gives genuine balanced modular congruence.

nodes.name: prime_field_zero_below_prime
nodes.summary: Zero is a canonical representative at every prime, including two.

nodes.name: prime_field_residue_reflexive
nodes.summary: Every bounded representative represents itself, including zero.

nodes.name: prime_field_residue_input_equal
nodes.summary: Equality transports the dividend of an actual residue graph.

nodes.name: prime_field_residue_congruence_transport
nodes.summary: Balanced congruence transports canonical residues; no quotient oracle is assumed.

nodes.name: prime_field_residue_bounded_value
nodes.summary: No two distinct representatives below p denote the same residue class.

nodes.name: prime_field_residue_modulus_zero
nodes.summary: The modulus itself has canonical residue zero, the characteristic-p boundary.

nodes.name: prime_field_add_exists
nodes.summary: Construct the unique canonical add output for every pair of residues.

nodes.name: prime_field_add_functional
nodes.summary: The actual bounded add graph is functional without any field-law premise.

nodes.name: prime_field_add_exists_unique
nodes.summary: Existence and uniqueness of canonical prime-field add are both proved.

nodes.name: prime_field_add_commutative
nodes.summary: Commutativity of actual canonical add, not an assumed table axiom.

nodes.name: prime_field_multiply_exists
nodes.summary: Construct the unique canonical multiply output for every pair of residues.

nodes.name: prime_field_multiply_functional
nodes.summary: The actual bounded multiply graph is functional without any field-law premise.

nodes.name: prime_field_multiply_exists_unique
nodes.summary: Existence and uniqueness of canonical prime-field multiply are both proved.

nodes.name: prime_field_multiply_commutative
nodes.summary: Commutativity of actual canonical multiply, not an assumed table axiom.

nodes.name: prime_field_add_associative
nodes.summary: Both bracketings of three canonical add operands give the same actual result.

nodes.name: prime_field_multiply_associative
nodes.summary: Both bracketings of three canonical multiply operands give the same actual result.

nodes.name: prime_field_left_distributive
nodes.summary: Actual left distributivity of multiplication over addition on bounded representatives.

nodes.name: prime_field_right_distributive
nodes.summary: Actual right distributivity of multiplication over addition on bounded representatives.

nodes.name: prime_field_add_zero_right
nodes.summary: Natural zero is the actual additive identity, not an arbitrary chosen code.

nodes.name: prime_field_add_zero_left
nodes.summary: Zero is also the left additive identity on every canonical representative.

nodes.name: prime_field_multiply_one_right
nodes.summary: Natural one is the actual multiplicative identity, including at p=2.

nodes.name: prime_field_multiply_one_left
nodes.summary: One is also the left multiplicative identity.

nodes.name: prime_field_multiply_zero_right
nodes.summary: Multiplication by the actual zero representative produces zero.

nodes.name: prime_field_multiply_zero_left
nodes.summary: Zero is absorbing on both sides of multiplication.

nodes.name: prime_field_add_cancel_left
nodes.summary: Additive cancellation follows from genuine balanced congruence cancellation and canonical bounds.

nodes.name: prime_field_negate_exists
nodes.summary: Construct a bounded additive inverse by actual signed floor division; the zero input is included.

nodes.name: prime_field_negate_functional
nodes.summary: Actual additive inverses are unique among canonical representatives.

nodes.name: prime_field_negate_exists_unique
nodes.summary: Every element, including zero, has a unique actual additive inverse.

nodes.name: prime_field_inverse_exists
nodes.summary: Every nonzero representative has an actual bounded multiplicative inverse, uniformly at every prime.

nodes.name: prime_field_inverse_functional
nodes.summary: Multiplicative inverses are unique as bounded natural representatives.

nodes.name: prime_field_inverse_exists_unique
nodes.summary: Proved unique inverse existence has exactly the nonzero carrier domain, not an odd-prime or supplied-inverse premise.

nodes.name: prime_field_zero_has_no_multiplicative_inverse
nodes.summary: Zero has no product equal to one; this follows from multiplication, not from the inverse definition's guard.

nodes.name: prime_field_inverse_output_nonzero
nodes.summary: An actual inverse is itself nonzero, so reciprocal inversion has the correct domain.

nodes.name: prime_field_inverse_symmetric
nodes.summary: Inversion is symmetric on the nonzero elements, with both domains proved.

nodes.name: prime_field_nonzero_coprime
nodes.summary: Every nonzero canonical element is genuinely coprime to its prime modulus.

nodes.name: prime_field_multiply_cancel_nonzero_left
nodes.summary: Cancellation by any nonzero element is proved, not assumed from a field certificate.

nodes.name: prime_field_no_zero_divisors
nodes.summary: A zero canonical product has a zero factor, including the characteristic-two case.

nodes.name: prime_field_residue_add
nodes.summary: The natural-number residue map preserves actual canonical add.

nodes.name: prime_field_residue_multiply
nodes.summary: The natural-number residue map preserves actual canonical multiply.

nodes.name: prime_field_positive_below_modulus_not_zero
nodes.summary: No positive natural below p has residue zero; the modulus boundary is sharp.

nodes.name: prime_field_arithmetic_laws
nodes.summary: Every prime has genuine canonical field arithmetic with distinct zero/one, total unique operations, both distributive laws, additive inverses and precisely nonzero multiplicative inverses.

nodes.name: prime_field_add_grid_value_exists
nodes.summary: Construct the actual bounded add value at every one of the p*p row-major indices.

nodes.name: prime_field_multiply_grid_value_exists
nodes.summary: Construct the actual bounded multiply value at every one of the p*p row-major indices.

nodes.name: prime_field_zero_extended_inverse_exists
nodes.summary: Totalize only the inverse table by recording zero at zero; the nonzero branch constructs a genuine inverse.

nodes.name: prime_field_zero_extended_inverse_functional
nodes.summary: The explicit zero convention and genuine nonzero inverses together define a functional total table operation.

nodes.name: prime_field_add_prefix_choice
nodes.summary: Ordinary finite induction codes actual pointwise add witnesses; no choice axiom or unproved field law is introduced.

nodes.name: prime_field_multiply_prefix_choice
nodes.summary: Ordinary finite induction codes actual pointwise multiply witnesses; no choice axiom or unproved field law is introduced.

nodes.name: prime_field_negate_prefix_choice
nodes.summary: Ordinary finite induction codes actual pointwise negate witnesses; no choice axiom or unproved field law is introduced.

nodes.name: prime_field_inverse_prefix_choice
nodes.summary: Ordinary finite induction codes actual pointwise inverse witnesses; no choice axiom or unproved field law is introduced.

nodes.name: prime_field_add_table_exists
nodes.summary: Construct every entry of the finite add table from primality alone.

nodes.name: prime_field_multiply_table_exists
nodes.summary: Construct every entry of the finite multiply table from primality alone.

nodes.name: prime_field_negate_table_exists
nodes.summary: Construct every entry of the finite negate table from primality alone.

nodes.name: prime_field_inverse_table_exists
nodes.summary: Construct every entry of the finite inverse table from primality alone.

nodes.name: prime_field_operation_tables_exists
nodes.summary: Every prime has four actual finite beta-coded arithmetic tables; zero is only a totalized inverse-table convention.

nodes.name: prime_field_add_grid_value_lookup
nodes.summary: Actual quotient/remainder uniqueness identifies both row-major coordinates of a add table entry.

nodes.name: prime_field_add_table_lookup
nodes.summary: Every decoded add table lookup has exactly the proved canonical arithmetic meaning.

nodes.name: prime_field_add_table_reflect
nodes.summary: Every genuine canonical add result occurs at its actual finite table index.

nodes.name: prime_field_multiply_grid_value_lookup
nodes.summary: Actual quotient/remainder uniqueness identifies both row-major coordinates of a multiply table entry.

nodes.name: prime_field_multiply_table_lookup
nodes.summary: Every decoded multiply table lookup has exactly the proved canonical arithmetic meaning.

nodes.name: prime_field_multiply_table_reflect
nodes.summary: Every genuine canonical multiply result occurs at its actual finite table index.

nodes.name: prime_field_negate_table_lookup
nodes.summary: Every decoded negate table lookup has its exact unary meaning, including the inverse-at-zero convention.

nodes.name: prime_field_negate_table_reflect
nodes.summary: Every genuine negate value is stored at its actual unary table index.

nodes.name: prime_field_inverse_table_lookup
nodes.summary: Every decoded inverse table lookup has its exact unary meaning, including the inverse-at-zero convention.

nodes.name: prime_field_inverse_table_reflect
nodes.summary: Every genuine inverse value is stored at its actual unary table index.

nodes.name: prime_field_add_table_commutative
nodes.summary: The actual finite add table is symmetric under exchanging row and column.

nodes.name: prime_field_add_table_associative
nodes.summary: Both parenthesizations of three actual add table lookups agree, with intermediate bounds proved.

nodes.name: prime_field_multiply_table_commutative
nodes.summary: The actual finite multiply table is symmetric under exchanging row and column.

nodes.name: prime_field_multiply_table_associative
nodes.summary: Both parenthesizations of three actual multiply table lookups agree, with intermediate bounds proved.

nodes.name: prime_field_inverse_table_zero
nodes.summary: The totalized inverse table really stores zero at zero, without claiming zero has an inverse.

nodes.name: prime_field_inverse_table_nonzero
nodes.summary: Every nonzero inverse-table entry multiplies its input to the actual one representative.

nodes.name: prime_field_left_table_distributive
nodes.summary: Actual finite addition and multiplication table entries satisfy left distributivity, with all intermediate bounds derived.

nodes.name: prime_field_right_table_distributive
nodes.summary: Actual finite addition and multiplication table entries satisfy right distributivity, with all intermediate bounds derived.

nodes.name: prime_field_enumeration_value
nodes.summary: Every decoded entry of the identity enumeration equals its actual index.

nodes.name: prime_field_enumeration_is_bijection
nodes.summary: The actual p-entry enumeration is bounded, injective and onto every canonical field representative.

nodes.name: prime_field_cardinality_exists
nodes.summary: Exactly p canonical elements are witnessed by an actual finite bijection, not an external model count.

nodes.name: prime_field_unit_trace_recode
nodes.summary: A genuine recoding preserving every one of the n+1 trace entries preserves all actual unit-addition steps.

nodes.name: prime_field_unit_trace_successor
nodes.summary: Append the genuinely computed next unit sum to an actual finite beta history.

nodes.name: prime_field_unit_trace_residue
nodes.summary: Ordinary induction proves that an actual n-step addition-of-one history has canonical residue n; the relation does not assume this invariant.

nodes.name: prime_field_unit_trace_result_bounded
nodes.summary: Every trace endpoint is a canonical representative, including the empty-history endpoint.

nodes.name: prime_field_unit_trace_exists
nodes.summary: Construct an actual history of n additions of one for every natural n, including the empty history.

nodes.name: prime_field_unit_multiple_residue
nodes.summary: An actual repeated sum of n ones has canonical residue n.

nodes.name: prime_field_unit_multiple_from_residue
nodes.summary: Construct a genuine repeated-addition history ending at any supplied canonical residue; the trace invariant is proved, not assumed.

nodes.name: prime_field_unit_multiple_functional
nodes.summary: Any two actual histories of the same number of additions of one have identical endpoints.

nodes.name: prime_field_unit_multiple_exists_unique
nodes.summary: Repeated addition is a total functional computation on every natural length, with an actual beta execution history.

nodes.name: prime_field_characteristic_exact
nodes.summary: The first positive number of additions of the actual identity one that returns zero is exactly p, including p=2.

nodes.name: prime_field_of_prime_order_exists
nodes.summary: For every prime construct all finite arithmetic tables, an exact p-element bijection, every field law, and characteristic p. This is the k=1 case only, not arbitrary prime-power extension fields.

nodes.name: Lt
nodes.summary: Witness-defined strict order on natural numbers.

nodes.name: Prime
nodes.summary: p is nonunit and every factorization of p has a unit factor.

nodes.name: Dvd
nodes.summary: The natural number d divides n.

nodes.name: Coprime
nodes.summary: Every common divisor of a and b is one.

nodes.name: DivRem
nodes.summary: q and r are a quotient and a strict remainder for n by d.

nodes.name: ModEq
nodes.summary: Balanced-natural congruence modulo m.

nodes.name: BetaAt
nodes.summary: x is the bounded beta-decoded value at index i.

nodes.name: BalancedInverse
nodes.summary: a times b is congruent to one modulo m.

nodes.name: BoundedNonzeroInverse
nodes.summary: a has a nonzero inverse strictly below m.

nodes.name: FpElement
nodes.summary: A prime modulus and an actual canonical natural representative a<p. Field laws are proved separately.

nodes.name: CanonicalModularResidue
nodes.summary: A strictly bounded canonical natural residue r<m together with exact balanced congruence to a modulo m.

nodes.name: FpAdd
nodes.summary: Bounded operands and the actual canonical residue of their natural sum. The old ND0023 residue graph is reused exactly.

nodes.name: FpMul
nodes.summary: Bounded operands and the actual canonical residue of their natural product; no multiplication law is assumed.

nodes.name: FpNeg
nodes.summary: An actual bounded additive inverse: FpAdd(p,a,b,0). Its existence and uniqueness are theorems.

nodes.name: FpInv
nodes.summary: An explicitly nonzero input and an actual product equal to canonical one. This relation never declares zero invertible.

nodes.name: FpFieldLaws
nodes.summary: The explicit conjunction of the actual canonical operations' field laws, including distinct zero/one and nonzero inverses. This is a proved conclusion, never an unproved constructor premise.

nodes.name: FpZeroExtendedInv
nodes.summary: The bounded nonzero inverse graph with an explicit zero-to-zero table convention. Zero is not asserted to be invertible.

nodes.name: FpAddGridValue
nodes.summary: An actual addition value at the row-major index i=a*p+b, with bounded coordinates supplied by FpAdd.

nodes.name: FpMulGridValue
nodes.summary: An actual multiplication value at the row-major index i=a*p+b; coordinate and value uniqueness are proved.

nodes.name: FpAddPrefix
nodes.summary: Every genuine beta entry below l gives the addition grid value at its actual index.

nodes.name: FpMulPrefix
nodes.summary: Every genuine beta entry below l gives the multiplication grid value at its actual index.

nodes.name: FpNegPrefix
nodes.summary: The actual beta prefix records an additive inverse for each index below l.

nodes.name: FpInvPrefix
nodes.summary: The actual beta prefix records the zero-extended inverse function. The nonzero inverse laws are separate theorems.

nodes.name: FpOperationTables
nodes.summary: Four constructed beta tables: p*p entries for addition and multiplication, and p entries for negation and zero-extended inversion. No field-law premise occurs in this graph.

nodes.name: IdentityMatrixSelector
nodes.summary: The actual beta-decoded coordinate list 0,1,…,l−1; its boundedness, injectivity, and full-matrix selection are proved separately.

nodes.name: FpCardinality
nodes.summary: The existing identity-selector beta graph together with explicit boundedness, injectivity and surjectivity onto all p canonical representatives. ND0141 is reused, not cloned.

nodes.name: FpUnitSteps
nodes.summary: Each consecutive pair of actual history entries is related by addition of the canonical one. No modular-residue invariant is assumed.

nodes.name: FpUnitTrace
nodes.summary: An actual beta history starts at zero, performs n additions of one and terminates at r. The residue invariant is established by induction.

nodes.name: FpUnitMultiple
nodes.summary: Existence of a genuine n-step addition-of-one history with endpoint r; this is not a restatement of divisibility or characteristic.

nodes.name: FpCharacteristic
nodes.summary: An actual p-step sum of one returns to zero, and no positive shorter such sum does. Its validity at every prime is proved from the trace invariant.

nodes.name: FpFiniteStructure
nodes.summary: The constructed prime-order structure combines actual operation tables, a p-element bijection, proved field laws and exact characteristic. Its existence is a theorem; extension fields of order p^k remain a separate open goal.
